original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected reproduction command and choose a single replay stage for profiling.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: The three `phases` steps (cells, chain, slots) of the cold frontier1042 replay that `make frontier1094-verify` runs as `baseline1042-cold`: does the merged exact sparse phase compiler (research/selected-replay-fastpath, previously measured only on the PR942 U8 word) reproduce their pinned CLIFFORD-RECIPES bytes from the archived canonical words, and how much faster is it than the pinned serial phases_full.py on the same machine?
scope_change_reason: The card asks for one measured replay bottleneck. The phases steps are 469 s of the recorded 1162 s frontier1042 run; PR1151 sped up the layer-end controls and explicitly left these steps unmeasured. This is the card's allowed variation (one stage), applied to existing merged tools rather than a new evaluator.
bottleneck_link: Side result for review throughput: a cold selected replay is the acceptance test for any new complex supplier built on the k8 chain; shortening it lets candidates be checked sooner. No mathematical claim.
stop_rule: Stop after byte-identity on all three pinned digests, a same-machine timing against the pinned serial step, and two corruption controls; do not edit or wire any manifest-pinned replay script.
evidence: verify.py: all three recipe files byte-identical to the k8 pins and the archived maintainer recipes, review fields (including the status, digests and adapter count the T16 binder asserts) equal; two corrupted words do not reproduce the pin. BENCHMARK-macos-arm64.json: same-machine wall times for pinned serial phases_full.py, the dense PR662 evaluator, the sparse evaluator and phases_parallel.py.
author: Josie Elliston (Claude Code research session)
ai_assistance: Prepared with Claude Code (Claude Opus); a Codex read-only review corrected the wiring notes, controls and credit. No subagents.

open_questions.question: Should the cold frontier1042 replay call the sparse compiler for its three phases steps?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The three steps are 469 s of the recorded 1162 s cold frontier1042 run; scaling the measured 12x sparse ratio, the run would lose about 430 s, and with PR1151 fall to roughly 300 s on the recorded machine.
open_questions.first_step: Give the three phases calls (reproduce_leaver.py, reproduce_leaver_chain.py, verify_slots.py) an engine option that runs research/selected-replay-fastpath/run.py into local/ and keeps every clifford_recipes_sha256 pin assertion.
open_questions.blocked_by: Maintainer decision: the scripts are manifest-pinned; reproduce_leaver_chain.py --skip-phases fails its whole-dictionary CHAIN-PINS check; verify_slots.py has no switch. Only the cells step can use --skip-phases plus an external pin check unchanged.

open_questions.question: Is the phase lowering still a bottleneck in other cold replays that call phases_full.py (23 byte-identical copies on main)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Every chain rebuild for a pending k8-based claim reruns the same lowering.
open_questions.first_step: Grep STAGES/STEPS receipts in research/*-audit archives for phases steps over 30 s and run this verifier pattern on their archived canonical words.
open_questions.blocked_by: Some archives may not retain the canonical word.
